name.text: Constructing an equation with given solutions

questiontext.text:
Find whole numbers \(p\), \(q\) and \(r\), with \(p \ne 0\), so that the solutions of \(p\sin^2 x + q\cos x + r = 0\) for \(0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ\) are exactly \(x \in {@setraw(tsols)@}\).

\(p =\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] \(\quad q =\) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] \(\quad r =\) [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Work backwards. The target angles are the solutions of [[if test="is(abs(u2) > 1)"]]\(\cos x = {@u1@}\) only (a factor such as \(\cos x = {@u2@}\) adds no angles, because \(\cos x\) is never more than 1).[[else]]\(\cos x = {@u1@}\) or \(\cos x = {@u2@}\).[[/if]] With \(c = \cos x\), a quadratic with roots \({@u1@}\) and \({@u2@}\) is \({@lead(-mp, "c^2")@}{@tm(mq, "c")@}{@tc(mp+mr)@} = 0\) (or any non-zero multiple of it).

Now replace \(c^2\) by \(1 - \sin^2 x\): \({@lead(-mp, "(1 - \\sin^2 x)")@}{@tm(mq, "\\cos x")@}{@tc(mp+mr)@} = 0\), that is \({@lead(mp, "\\sin^2 x")@}{@tm(mq, "\\cos x")@}{@tc(mr)@} = 0\).

One answer is \(p = {@mp@}\), \(q = {@mq@}\), \(r = {@mr@}\). Any non-zero multiple, such as \(p = {@2*mp@}\), \(q = {@2*mq@}\), \(r = {@2*mr@}\), also works.

questiondescription.text:
Trigonometry III: constructing an equation with given solutions

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.5: Find whole numbers p, q, r so that p sin^2 x + q cos x + r = 0 has a given solution set in 0 to 360 degrees.

Core

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: \(p\) must not be 0: the equation must contain \(\sin^2 x\).

There is a sign slip where \(\sin^2 x\) and \(\cos^2 x\) are exchanged. With your numbers, \({@ans1@}\sin^2 x = {@ans1@}(1 - c^2)\) where \(c = \cos x\), so the equation becomes \({@-ans1*c^2+ans2*c+(ans1+ans3)@} = 0\), whose solutions are \(x \in {@setraw(lsol)@}\).

falsefeedback.text: With your numbers the equation becomes \({@-ans1*c^2+ans2*c+(ans1+ans3)@} = 0\) with \(c = \cos x\), and its solutions are \(x \in {@setraw(lsol)@}\) (no solutions if this is empty). Work backwards: which values of \(\cos x\) give the target angles? Build a quadratic in \(c\) with those roots, then replace \(c^2\) by \(1 - \sin^2 x\).

qtest.description: Correct: a multiple of the model
